title: [ROCm][Perf] gfx950 device length aware top-k split policy for k=2048
bodyExcerpt:
This fixes #55327.

The change generalizes `topKPerRowDecodeGfx950DeviceLengthAware` to work with different values of k, and adds `gfx950TopK2048ActiveBlocks`. The grid still only depends on `numRows`, so graph capture stays stable, and the number of splits is now determined on device per row, ensuring that there are at least 2048 real indices in each split. Rows under 4096 can be processed by a single block, skipping the merge step.

GLM-5.2 and GLM-5.3 use `index_topk` 2048, which goes through the generic path on gfx950 and has 10 splits. In the merge step, all 20480 candidates are processed by a single block for each row. For rows with fewer active tokens this can lead to significant overhead. With this PR, the number of candidates per row in the merge step will be reduced to between 0 and 12288, a 70 percent reduction in the median case.

I also added two new tests for gfx950 and k 2048, to make sure we're covering the different numbers of splits and graph capture and replay.

I've checked this with a CPU model on all 35 shapes mentioned in the issue, and the result is an exact match with exact top-k for all of them. The kernel compiles fine for gfx950, and I'll provide timings on MI355X in this PR.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Fall back to free text in the GLM-4.7 structural tag without function tools
bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

Since #56403, every GLM-4.7 request with tools gets the shallow structural tag by default. A Responses request whose tools are all builtin (`mcp`, `web_search`, ...) has no function tool to build a tag for, so the builder emits `TriggeredTagsFormat(tags=[])`, which xgrammar rejects. Such requests now fail with `400 Invalid structural tag specification` instead of generating text as they did before #56403.

## Claims

- GLM-4.7 (`glm_4_7` structural tag model, also used by `ling3`) with `tool_choice="auto"` and no function tools falls back to free text, as the xgrammar builtin and the `hermes` tag already do.
- No change for requests with at least one function tool, or for `required` / named tool choice.

## Validation

Repro on `main` (CPU only):

```python
from unittest.mock import MagicMock
import vllm.envs as envs; envs.VLLM_ENFORCE_STRICT_TOOL_CALLING = True
from vllm.parser.abstract_parser import DelegatingParser

title: [Feature][DCP] --dcp-gather: gather-based DCP for MLA attention without native DCP (+ DSv4)
bodyExcerpt:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Draft: `--dcp-gather` runs DCP for MLA models whose attention can't run it natively.
- It keeps the native block-sharded KV layout and pulls each layer's pages into a shared scratch cache, so attention backends need no DCP support.
- The pull runs on a side stream through symmetric memory, overlapped with the previous layer's output projection and MoE.
- It is an alternative to layer-sharded KV (KVPP, #59059). DeepSeek-V4, which has no native DCP, always uses it.

Related fixes split out:
- #59951: DCP group rank order, needed for DCP groups that span TP × PCP.
- #59961: DSv3.2 top-k across PP stages, needed for correct PP results.

## Claims

- **New configs.** `-dcp N --dcp-gather` works where native DCP doesn't. Examples: GLM-5.3 at TP2/TP4 (FlashMLA sparse needs fewer than 32 local heads and `ag_rs`), dense MLA under PCP, and DeepSeek-V4. Attention backends are unmodified.
- **GLM-5.3-NVFP4 prefill throughput.**
  - Within 0.5% of KVPP where KV fits, and 23% faster where KV is tight.
  - 10% more KV capacity than KVPP.
  - At TP4, 1.56x native TP4 × DCP4.
- **No global side effects.** The pull uses no NCCL, so the model's all-reduce backends (custom, FlashInfer, symmetric memory) stay enabled.
- **DeepSeek-V4-Flash** DCP at TP2/TP4 matches baseline accuracy.

## Validation

GSM8K (5-shot) on 4x B300, MRV2. PP rows also include #59961.

| model | config | baseline (no DCP) | `--dcp-gather` |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| GLM-5.3-NVFP4 | TP4 `-dcp 4` | - | 0.905 (200 q) |
| GLM-5.3-NVFP4 | TP1 × PCP4 × EP4 `-dcp 4` | 0.890 (200 q) | 0.920 (200 q) |
| GLM-5.3-NVFP4 | TP2 × PCP2 `-dcp 4` | 0.905 (native DCP with #59951) | 0.904 (500 q) |
| GLM-5.3-NVFP4 | PP2 × TP2 `-dcp 2` | 0.908 (1319 q) | 0.895 (200 q) |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash | TP2 `-dcp 2` | 0.952 (500 q) | 0.958 (500 q) |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash | TP4 `-dcp 4` | - | 0.950 (500 q) |

bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

GLM-5.3-Flash P/D over Mooncake fails: its kpool indexer stores several kernel blocks in one tensor row and keeps its kpool tail inside the same allocation, which #53906 taught NIXL but not Mooncake. This PR gives Mooncake the same handling, sharing NIXL's helpers.

- GLM-5.3-Flash prefill/decode over Mooncake works: chat GSM8K 0.970 (0.974 with MTP), against 0.972 for a single server, with no failed transfers. Before this PR most transfers failed and requests errored.
- Other models keep their registration: the change only applies to a compressed cache whose rows hold several kernel blocks, the same predicate NIXL uses.

## Overview

Move the FlashInfer MLA decode workspaces (sparse trtllm-gen/cute-dsl, dense MLA, DSV4/DSV4.1 sparse) from module-global `torch.zeros` tensors into `WorkspaceManager` scratch. Part of #59055; with #59156 the memory is then released by `/sleep`.

- The DCP sizing (`_required_workspace_bytes`) and `VLLM_FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_BUFFER_SIZE` override are unchanged.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Bound sparse indexer decode workspace at layer build time
bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

ROCm-only alternative to #58014 for #55132. The ROCm sparse-MLA indexer works out its decode-row bound when the layer is built and passes it to the ROCm ops, instead of reading the vLLM config during the profiling run. `gpu_worker.py` is not changed.

title: [Bug]: RecoverSSM align mode commits the final SSM state to an unwritten block at exact block boundaries (floor vs ceil-1)
bodyExcerpt:
### Your current environment

Reproduced on a downstream fork, not on stock vLLM: Morrowmake/vllm-cmp170hx 1.7.0 (`v0.30.1rc1.dev368+gc1ce6491e`). It routes GLM-5 KDA layers through the Kimi-K3 RecoverSSM kernels. 4× SM80 GPUs (CMP 170HX, 64 GB), TP4, DFlash spec decode, prefix caching on (`mamba_cache_mode=align`), Mamba block size 1152.

Both affected lines are unchanged on `main` @ 0872ddf4b96d.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

In align mode, RecoverSSM puts the final committed state in column `floor(x / B)`. The rest of the align path uses `ceil(x / B) - 1`:

- `vllm/v1/worker/mamba_utils.py:1482`: `prev_state_idx = (num_computed_tokens - 1) // block_size`
- `vllm/v1/worker/mamba_utils.py:467`: `dest_block_idx = aligned_new_computed // block_size - 1`

The two RecoverSSM sites:

- `vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/ops/recoverssm.py:287` (`_prepare_commit_plan_kernel`): `final_num_computed // mamba_block_size`
- `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_states/recoverssm.py:97` (`_postprocess_recoverssm_align_kernel`): `(num_computed + num_sampled) // MAMBA_BLOCK_SIZE`

The two conventions agree except when `x` is an exact multiple of `B`. There they differ, and that happens when a verify step ends exactly on a block boundary with all drafts accepted. RecoverSSM then commits the state to column `k`, while the next step reads its recurrent and conv state from a block this request never wrote. New Mamba blocks are not zeroed (#56524), so the state is garbage, or another request's state.

Observed effect: generation loses context mid-word a few tokens after a multiple of 1152, then repeats a token until `max_tokens` (`…Inputhandlehandlehandle…`, `locklocklock…`).

Found and diagnosed by @YulHeon in Morrowmake/glm53-flash-cmp170hx-recipe#7, which has the boundary-position analysis.

**Proposed fix**: use `ceil - 1` in both places. It does not change anything when `x` is not a multiple of `B`.

--- a/vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/ops/recoverssm.py
+++ b/vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/ops/recover

title: [Bugfix][DSv3.2] Carry the shared indexer top-k across pipeline stages
bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

Fix a GSM8K accuracy loss on GLM-5.x / DeepSeek-V3.2-style models under pipeline parallelism. These models reuse the previous layer's indexer top-k, and when a PP stage starts on a reusing layer, that stage read a stale top-k. This PR sends the top-k along with the intermediate tensors.

## Claims

- GLM-5.3-NVFP4 PP2 × TP2 on main: GSM8K 0.879 → 0.908. Before the fix, stage 1's first three layers attend with the previous step's top-k.
- With gather-based DCP (#59916), where it was more visible: 0.820 → 0.908.
- Only stage boundaries that land on a top-k-reusing layer send anything extra (`(num_tokens, index_topk)` int32 per step). Other models and partitions are unchanged.

## Validation

GSM8K (5-shot, all 1319 q) on 4x B300, MRV2, GLM-5.3-NVFP4, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla -cc.cudagraph_mode=NONE`:

| config | main | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| `-pp 2 -tp 2` | 0.879 | 0.908 |
| `-pp 2 -tp 2 -dcp 2` with gather DCP (#59916) | 0.820 | 0.908 |
| same, `VLLM_PP_LAYER_PARTITION=38,40` (boundary aligned to a top-k group), no fix | 0.882 | - |

## Details

**Root cause.** GLM-5.3 sets `index_topk_freq=4` with offset 3, so groups of layers reuse the top-k computed by the group's first layer.
- The default PP2 split puts the stage boundary at layer 39, which is inside a group.
- Stage 1's first layers (39-41) therefore skip the indexer and read `topk_indices_buffer`. On that stage the buffer holds the top-k of the previous step's last indexer layer, for the previous batch.
- Aligning the partition (38/40) restored accuracy, which confirms the cause.

**Fix.** `reuses_previous_topk(config, layer_id)` is factored out of the attention init.
- The model adds `topk_indices` to its intermediate tensors when any stage starts on a reusing layer.
- The receiving stage copies it into its top-k buffer.

Only the NVIDIA `deepseek_v32` model path is patched. The AMD path has the same structure and could get the same fix in a follow-up.

**Duplicate check.** No open PR

title: [Bugfix][Core] Retire stale Mamba spec blocks in prefill checkpoint steps
bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

With MTP and prefix caching on, hybrid models such as GLM-5.3-Flash can return garbage when a request reuses a cached prompt prefix. Some prefill steps save a checkpoint of the linear-attention state in the middle of a chunk. In those steps the scheduler leaves an unused MTP scratch block in the slot that belongs to the checkpoint. That block is never written, yet it is registered in the prefix cache ahead of the real checkpoint, so later requests resume from it. This change moves the scratch block out of the way in those steps too, as already happens in every other step.

The skip was added together with internal checkpoints in #53614. GLM-5.3-Flash reaches this path since #56960. The branch is based on current main (58b3298457). No open PR changes speculative-block relocation; #57128 changes the Mamba lookup and does not touch this path.

## Claims

- Fixes persistent garbage output after prefix-cache hits for hybrid models with internal prefill checkpoints and MTP, for example GLM-5.3-Flash with `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1}'`.
- No behavior change without speculative decoding, for `mamba_cache_mode` other than `align`, or for steps without an internal checkpoint.

## Validation

Setup: RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 on 2 H200 GPUs, served with default settings plus MTP:

```
vllm serve RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
    --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 1}'
```

Reproducer (script below): send a long prompt while another long prompt is still being processed, then send the exact same prompt again. The second request reuses the cached start of the prompt.

- Before the fix, the second answer was garbage in 3 of 3 trials, for example `File: /home/erdos/2024/4/4  # File: /home/erdos/2024/4/4 ...`, while the first answer was a normal list of function names.
- With the fix, both answers were normal in 3 of 3 trials.

title: perf: route GLM-5.2 fused-QKV-A GEMM through dsv3_fused_a_gemm on SM10x
bodyExcerpt:
## Summary

This PR routes the GLM-5.2 (GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM) fused QKV-A projection
through the existing `min_latency_fused_qkv_a_proj` custom op backed by
`dsv3_fused_a_gemm`, eliminating the cuBLASLt split-K + splitKreduce kernel pair
at decode batch size 1. The `dsv3_fused_a_gemm` C++ kernel already supports the
GLM-5.2 fused-QKV-A shape with a warp-specialized fused-A kernel that folds the
split-K reduction inside the CTA -- the same kernel SGLang uses for this projection.
The custom op has a registered `fake_impl`, making it torch.compile-safe and CUDA-graph
capture-safe.

The core change widens `_can_use_min_latency_fused_qkv_a_gemm` to accept the
GLM-5.2 fused-QKV-A weight shape alongside the existing DeepSeek-V3 shape. This
collapses two kernel launches per layer (splitK GEMM + splitKreduce) into a single
`fused_a_gemm_kernel` launch. PDL (Programmatic Dependent Launch) is also enabled on
SM90+ for additional latency reduction at low token counts.

Because the fused-QKV-A custom-op path is frozen into the CUDA graph at capture time,
the GLM-5.2 branch is gated on the `VLLM_DISABLE_GLM52_LOW_LATENCY_GEMM`
kill switch so the feature-toggle A/B comparison captures the full benefit of this path
(the DeepSeek-V3 shape stays always-on). Without this gate the toggle only disabled the
secondary CuTe-DSL projections and the A/B delta collapsed to noise.

The GLM-5.2 low-latency GEMM module is also updated: the device capability gate is
widened from SM103-only to the full SM10x family (covering B200/SM100), the dead
`GLM52_Q_B_PROJECTION` spec is replaced with `GLM52_DENSE_GATE_UP_PROJECTION`
for the dense MLP layers, and an environment variable kill-switch is added for safe A/B
testing.

## Performance Results

Measured on nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 with 4x B200 (SM100, TP=4), bs=1,

title: [Bugfix][DCP] Sort DCP group ranks so rank_in_group matches collective order
bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

Fix garbage output when a DCP group spans TP × PCP (e.g. TP2 × PCP2 × DCP4): sort each DCP group's ranks so `rank_in_group` agrees with the order collectives return shards in.

## Claims

- TP2 × PCP2 × DCP4 on GLM-5.3-NVFP4 goes from GSM8K 0.000 to 0.905.
- No change for DCP groups that were already ascending (DCP within TP, or DCP == PCP), which covers every previously validated configuration.

## Validation

GSM8K (5-shot) on 4x B300, MRV2, GLM-5.3-NVFP4, `-tp 2 -pcp 2 -dcp 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla -cc.cudagraph_mode=NONE`:

| | GSM8K |
|---|---:|
| main | 0.000 |
| this PR | 0.905 |

```bash
pytest tests/distributed/test_dcp_a2a.py -k test_dcp_group_ranks_match_collective_order  # 5 passed
```

## Details

**Root cause.** With PCP, `initialize_model_parallel` builds a DCP group that spans TP × PCP PCP-first (`all_ranks.transpose(-1, -2)`), giving member lists like `[0, 2, 1, 3]`.
- `torch.distributed.new_group` sorts its ranks, so all-gathers return shards in global-rank order.
- `GroupCoordinator.rank_in_group` is `ranks.index(rank)` on the unsorted list.
- The DCP LSE merge (`correct_attn_out`) uses `rank_in_group` to pick this rank's LSE from the gathered LSEs. So DCP ranks 1 and 2 rescaled their partial outputs with each other's LSE.

This was found by comparing each rank's attention partials against a torch reference and merging them offline: every rank's partials were correct and only the merge was wrong. The new unit test checks that DCP groups are ascending for TP-only, PCP-only and TP × PCP layouts.

**Duplicate check.** No open PR touches DCP group rank order (searched "dcp rank order", "DCP group ranks").

title: [Bugfix][Quantization] NVFP4 linear: keep each fused shard's global weight scale
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`KNvfp4Static.process` runs a fused NVFP4 linear (`q/k/v`, `gate/up`) under the max of its shards' global weight scales (`weight_scale_2`), and only warns when they differ. Every smaller shard is then dequantized `gs_max / gs_shard` times too large. ModelOpt quantizes each projection with its own per-tensor amax, so fused shards often do differ.

Example: `tiyuvta/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4` (ModelOpt 0.46.0 W4A16) quantizes the shared experts and dense MLPs. Their gate/up global scales differ in nearly every MoE layer, with up/gate ratios from 0.46 to 2.51 across a layer sample, so one projection is inflated by up to 2.5x in every layer for every token. Greedy output stays coherent, which is why this hides. Sampled output at the checkpoint's own defaults (temperature 1, top_p 0.95) degenerates into multilingual word salad within a few hundred tokens.

## Changes

- `_reconcile_nvfp4_shard_global_scales`: before the shared max is taken, each smaller shard's e4m3 block scales are multiplied by `gs_shard / gs_max`.
  - The factor is at most 1, so block scales cannot overflow.
  - Each shard keeps its effective dequant scale within e4m3 rounding.
  - The FP4 payload is unchanged.
- Shared-scale checkpoints are bit-exact no-ops. The previous warning remains for layers whose shard widths (`logical_widths`) cannot be verified against `weight_scale`.
- This is the same policy as FP8's `requantize_with_max_scale` for fused linears, and as #55073 for NVFP4 MoE w13. #55073 does not touch the linear path.

- #47515 fixes the same problem for **compressed-tensors** NVFP4 linears (`compressed_tensors_w4a4_nvfp4.py`). It is exact for two-partition layers, using a per-partition multiply on the GEMM output at runtime. This PR covers the **ModelOpt** path (`KNvfp4Static`, shared by W4A4 and W4A16), which #47515 does not touch. title: [Bugfix][Model] GLM-5.x: load ModelOpt NVFP4 MLA projections into BF16 fused_qkv_a_proj
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`fused_qkv_a_proj` in GLM-5.x (`glm5next`) is always BF16, and the loader only knows how to dequantize FP8 checkpoints into it (`_try_load_fp8_attn_proj`). A ModelOpt NVFP4 checkpoint that also quantizes the MLA projections stores `q_a_proj` and `kv_a_proj_with_mqa` as a packed e2m1 `weight` (uint8), an e4m3 per-16 `weight_scale` and an fp32 `weight_scale_2`. Those tensors have no matching parameter, so loading fails:

```
vllm/model_executor/parameter.py, in load_merged_column_weight
    assert param_data.shape == loaded_weight.shape
AssertionError
```

Example checkpoint: `tiyuvta/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4` (ModelOpt 0.46.0 W4A16; MoE experts, dense MLPs and the MLA `q_a`/`q_b`/`kv_a`/`o` projections are NVFP4; KDA, `kv_b_proj`, routers and norms stay BF16).

## Changes

- `_try_load_nvfp4_attn_proj`: buffers `weight`, `weight_scale` and `weight_scale_2` per projection, then dequantizes with the existing `dequantize_to_dtype(..., swizzle=False)` and loads the BF16 result into the fused shard. It only acts when the target has no `weight_scale` param, so projections the model keeps in NVFP4 (here `q_b_proj`, `o_proj`) load as before.
- Called before the FP8 path in both the main model and the MTP layer, because the FP8 path now also accepts `.weight_scale` (Quark). It only claims uint8 weights and e4m3 scales, so FP8 and BF16 tensors are untouched.
- The NoPE `kv_a` row padding and fused-shard load move into a small shared helper, `_load_bf16_attn_proj`, used by both paths.

## Not a duplicate

No open or merged PR or issue covers NVFP4 MLA projections in the GLM-5.x loader (searched `fused_qkv_a_proj nvfp4`, `glm5next nvfp4 q_a_proj`, `kv_a_proj_with_mqa nvfp4`, the assertion text). The scale mismatch in NVFP4 MoE experts (#54974, #55073) is a separate issue.

Structured output skipped a reasoning-end token that is also content, such as GLM's `<tool_call>` with no `</think>` before it. title: [Bugfix][Quark] Pass grouped-routing arguments to OCP MX monolithic kernels
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`QuarkOCP_MX_MoEMethod.apply_monolithic` does not forward `num_expert_group`, `topk_group`, `e_score_correction_bias` or `routed_scaling_factor` to the monolithic kernel, so the kernel falls back to their defaults.

Quark OCP MX picks its experts through `select_mxfp4_moe_backend`, the same path `Mxfp4MoEMethod` uses. `Mxfp4MoEMethod` has forwarded these four arguments since #50000; the Quark copy, added earlier in #38774, was never updated.

**Who is affected.** The bug needs three things at once:

1. A Quark **weight-only MXFP4 (`w_mxfp4`, W4A16)** checkpoint.
2. DeepSeek-V3/V4-style routing (grouped top-k and/or a correction bias with a scaling factor).
3. A **monolithic** MXFP4 kernel. On SM100, the BF16-activation priority list selects `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_BF16` (`TrtLlmMxfp4ExpertsMonolithic`, which supports `DeepSeekV3` routing) by default. On ROCm, `AiterW4A16ExpertsMonolithic` (`DeepSeekV3`/`DeepseekV4`) is used when requested explicitly.

In that setup the kernel routes with `n_group=0`, `topk_group=0` and no bias, and the scaling factor is `None` (TRT-LLM) or 1.0 (aiter).

The published Quark MXFP4 MoE checkpoints are W4A4: `amd/DeepSeek-R1-MXFP4`, `amd/DeepSeek-R1-0528-MXFP4`, `amd/Kimi-K2.5-MXFP4`, `amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4`, `amd/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-MXFP4` and others. W4A4 resolves to the modular `AiterExperts` on ROCm and to emulation on CUDA, so routing happens in vLLM's router with every argument. As far as I can tell, no public checkpoint hits this today. This PR fixes a latent inconsistency before a W4A16 export does.

This PR forwards the four arguments exactly as `Mxfp4MoEMethod` does. Models without grouped routing pass `None` or the default values and are unaffected.

## Test Plan

- `pre-commit` (ruff, mypy).
- Code-path analysis above (`oracle/mxfp4.py` activation filtering and priority lists). There is no public W4A16 Quark checkpoint to run end to end.

## Test Result

`pre-commit` passes. Related: #59757 moves the monolithic kernel

title: [Bug][ROCm] GLM-5.3-Flash: recent-context pools not guaranteed in kpool top-k selection (always_select_tail covers only the incomplete pool)
bodyExcerpt:
### TL;DR

On GLM-5.3-Flash (kpool sparse indexer, ROCm aiter path), per-layer top-k selection frequently drops the most recent context pools at long prompt lengths — even with a correct block table. The config sets `always_select_tail=True`, but the only tail the selection machinery guarantees is the ≤3-token *incomplete* pool; complete recent pools compete in the top-k like everything else and can rank below the `index_topk=2048` cutoff. Tail-of-context retrieval then fails non-deterministically. Forcing the last 128 pools (512 tokens, 25% of the budget) into every layer's selection fixed all our failing lengths up to the full 256K context.

### Setup

GLM-5.3-Flash-AWQ-W4A16, vLLM `0.31.0.dev0+git73859fec` (Sep-28 pin), TP=2 (ray across 2× AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 / Strix Halo, gfx1151), aiter sparse MLA, `index_topk` 2048, `index_kpool` 4, `max_model_len` 262144. Probe: needle ("Paris") in the final line, a single neutral decoy ("Berlin") in the first line, forced tool-call response, lengths 12K–255K prompt tokens.

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Reject cudagraph_mode=FULL at startup
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

HiSparse cannot capture prefill or mixed batches in CUDA graphs. It picks its prefill path from per-step page residency (resident pages, or spilled pages staged from host), and it mirrors prefill KV to host outside the graph. With `cudagraph_mode=FULL`, a backend reporting `ALWAYS` support (FlashInfer sparse MLA on SM100) has prefill/mixed batches captured as FULL graphs. A replay could then take the branch frozen at capture and skip the host mirror.

## Changes

HiSparse rejects `cudagraph_mode=FULL` at config validation, next to its other unsupported-config checks (PP, DCP). The error points to `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` (the default), which keeps FULL graphs for decode batches. Being a config check, it covers every backend HiSparse runs on.

Separately, `FULL` with FlashInfer sparse MLA on SM100 currently crashes on prefill replay even without HiSparse: #59681.

### Summary

GLM-5.3-Flash (`glm5_next`) fails to start with any EAGLE-family drafter whose layers are plain sliding-window attention (e.g. the block-diffusion DFlash2 drafter, 5 GQA `SlidingWindowSpec` layers). `_get_kv_cache_groups_glm5_next` only accepts exact `MLAAttentionSpec` in the attention group, so it declines; the generic page-size unification then cannot pad the DSA indexer (MLA family) and startup dies:

title: [Bugfix] Keep the GLM-5.3 kpool tail and Qwen4 QSA ring out of the null block
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Block id 0 is the null block. It is shared by every KV cache group and is assumed to stay zero. Since #35431, the runners mark rows that own no state with 0 in the block table, not `PAD_SLOT_ID`: dummy runs, CUDA graph capture and padding rows all carry 0. Two ring caches that address their pages through column 0 of the block table did not treat 0 as "no ring", so dummy runs wrote their rows into block 0:

- **GLM-5.3-Flash kpool tail:** `_kpool_tail_slot_mapping_kernel` maps every token to `block_table[req][0] * kpool + pos % kpool`. Its torch fallback does the same.
- **Qwen4 QSA circular ring:** `circular_qsa_slot_mapping` and `_build_qsa_metadata_kernel` map tokens to `block_table[req, 0]` and kept every block `>= 0`. The compressed QSA path already keeps dummy slots inert (`test_qsa_compressed_metadata_keeps_dummy_slots_inert`); the ring path did not.

Every scheduled request owns its ring block, so a request on the null block has none. Its tokens now map to PAD, as the generic slot mapping does. The ring writers already skip PAD slots.

This is the same pattern as #58560, which fixes the DeepSeek-V4.1 compressor ring.

## Changes

- `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py`: the kpool tail slot mapping (Triton and torch) emits PAD for requests on the null block.
- `vllm/models/qwen4_exp/common/qsa_cache.py`: the QSA circular ring slot mapping (torch and Triton) requires block `> 0`.
- Tests: the existing QSA circular metadata test, which runs the Triton builder, also checks a dummy batch (all-zero block table) and expects PAD. QSA tests that used block 0 as a real ring block now start real blocks at 1. This includes `_make_block_table` in the pre-indexer test, which could randomly hand out block 0. The kpool tail change has no new test: its unit tests run the torch fallback on CPU, while production only takes the Triton kernel. It was checked by hand on both paths.

title: [KV Offload] Give each rank its own CPU region outside the replicated layout
bodyExcerpt:
Outside the replicated layout, ranks never read each other's slots, but they still share one region whose rows interleave all ranks. Every rank pre-faults and pins its strided slots in the same shm file, contending with the others.

Give each rank its own region holding only its slots, in its own shm file. No other process maps that file, so the rank no longer waits on the cross-worker barrier before unlinking it. The replicated layout keeps the shared region.

title: [KV Offload] Split the CPU offload region across shm files
bodyExcerpt:
Pre-faulting the CPU offload region is capped by its single `/dev/shm` file: page-cache inserts into one shmem file are serialized, so more workers or threads stop helping. On one H200 node, eight processes pre-faulting disjoint parts of a 64 GiB file reach 9.8 GiB/s in total. Given one file each, they reach 24.6 GiB/s, and sixteen files reach 44.8 GiB/s. #59430 hits the same ceiling with threads.

Split the region's rows over up to 32 files of at least 1 GiB each. The files are mapped back to back over one anonymous reservation, so the region stays contiguous. Workers with per-rank slots start pre-faulting on different files. Regions under 2 GiB, and other users of `SharedOffloadRegion`, keep a single file.

## Tests

4× H200, measured on `16d4ac4ba3` with this change (the touched files are unchanged on current main):

- GLM-5.3 W4A8, TP4 + EP, 256 GiB native CPU offload: the offload startup step fell from 63.6 to 38.3 s, and pre-faulting from 42.8 to 19.4 s. A 20k-token retrieval prompt answered 8/8 lookups cold and 8/8 after `/reset_prefix_cache`, with 3.9 GB reloaded from CPU.

title: [KV Offload] Split replicated-layout pre-faulting across workers

title: [KV Offload] Pin only each worker's own offload slots
bodyExcerpt:
Outside the replicated layout, each worker only uses its own slot of every row in the shared CPU region, yet every worker `cudaHostRegister`s the whole region. At TP4, every page gets pinned four times.

Register only the worker's slot of each row, rounded out to pages. The replicated layout keeps whole-region registration. So do slots within a page of the full row and regions over 65,536 rows, where per-call overhead would dominate.

TieringOffloadingSpec workers pin through the same path, so they get this too. #59430 lists this redundant pinning as a follow-up, and no open PR changes it.

## Tests
